title: [TPU/PD Diagnostic] --disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum is CUDA-only: on TPU the prefill engine passes health checks and then every rank dies on the first real request (assert kv_page_indices_gpu.is_cuda)
body:
### Checklist

- [ ] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [ ] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Summary

The P/D transfer checksum (`--disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum`, Adler-32 over each request's KV pages on the prefill, verified on the decode) is documented as "Enable on both prefill and decode engines" with no platform restriction. On TPU it cannot work and it fails in the worst possible way: the prefill engine starts, loads weights, compiles, answers `/health` and `/health_generate` (health-check requests skip the checksum and send `0`), and then the first real request kills all eight scheduler ranks with

```
  File ".../sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py", line 1418, in send_kv_chunk
  File ".../sglang/srt/disaggregation/checksum.py", line 105, in compute
    assert kv_page_indices_gpu.is_cuda and kv_page_indices_gpu.is_contiguous()
AssertionError
```

Reproduced on gpt-oss-120b and on Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B (identical traceback on all ranks of both). The checksum computer is constructed with `torch.device("cuda:…")`, asserts `is_cuda` on its inputs and calls the CUDA Adler-32 kernels in `sglang.kernels.ops.memory.adler32`; there is no TPU implementation and no validation that rejects the flag on `--device tpu`.

**Expected behavior.** Either a TPU implementation of the strided Adler-32 (or a host-side fallback), or an argument-validation error on TPU.
A monitoring option must never let an engine pass its health checks and then die on the first user request.\

## Fix proposal

1. **Reject up front.** In argument validation, `disaggregation_enable_kv_checksum` with `device == "tpu"` → `ValueError` naming the flag,
   until a TPU implementation exists. Also skip the `torch.device("cuda:…")` construction on non-CUDA devices.
2. **Implement for TPU.** The checksum only needs the page bytes of one request; a host-side Adler-32 over the pages gathered from the TPU  pool (or a Pallas kernel) would make the transfer check usable where it matters most, on a new transport backend (raiden). Until then, the only transfer-integrity evidence on TPU is the differential test against the monolithic server.
3. **Never die on a per-request failure.** As with our other reports (F-5, F-8, F-10), an exception while post-processing one request should fail that request, not the scheduler.

### Reproduction


1. Start a gpt-oss-120b P/D pair on TPU with `--disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum` on both engines (any other flags as in a working recipe).
2. Wait for `LB /health_generate ready`.
3. Send one normal request: `curl -s $LB/generate -d '{"text":"hello","sampling_params":{"max_new_tokens":8}}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'`.
4. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' $PREFILL/health`.

**Observed.** Step 3 returns an error after the proxy timeout; step 4 returns `000`; the prefill log shows the assertion on every rank.
**Expected.** Step 3 answers; or the server refuses to start with "kv checksum is not supported on TPU".

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| sglang-torchtpu | `main` @ 09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709 (2026-10-07), sglang 0.5.13.dev7249 |
| TPU stack | torch-tpu 0.1.1+release.2026.9.22.20260927223741, libtpu 0.0.47, tpu-sync-torch 0.0.1.dev20261002213151, torch 2.11.0+cpu, transformers 5.8.1 |
| Hardware | Two TPU v7x hosts (4 chips / 8 TensorCores each), prefill on host a, decode on host b, TP 8, EP 8, raiden transfer |
| Flags that trigger it | `--disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum` on both engines (Config A recipe otherwise; `--kv-canary none`) |
| Models | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (MXFP4, fp8 KV, page 64); `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct` (bf16, fp8 KV, page 128) |

title: [TPU/Compile] --kv-canary cannot start any engine on TPU: the canary pool patcher has no attacher for TpuFusedMHATokenToKVPool (NotImplementedError) and the SWA adapter assumes separate k_buffer/v_buffer (AttributeError); both crash all ranks at start-up
body:
### Checklist

- [ ] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [ ] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Summary

The KV canary (`--kv-canary log|raise`) is the build's own detector for use-after-free and overlapping page writes in the KV pool. On TPU it cannot be enabled: every scheduler rank dies during memory-pool set-up, 6 s after `Load weight end`, the launcher kills the process group, and the server never comes up. Reproduced on both of our models, with two different failures that have the same root cause:

| Model | Top-level pool class | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-120b (hybrid sliding window) | `SWAKVPool` → attacher `attach_swa` | the SWA adapter reads `sub_pool.k_buffer[0]` on each sub-pool; the TPU sub-pools are `TpuFusedMHATokenToKVPool`, which keeps one fused 5-D `kv_buffer` and has no `k_buffer`/`v_buffer` → `AttributeError: 'TpuFusedMHATokenToKVPool' object has no attribute 'k_buffer'. Did you mean: 'kv_buffer'?` |
| Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B (full attention) | `TpuFusedMHATokenToKVPool` | the attacher registry is keyed by exact type and knows only the generic pool classes → `NotImplementedError: kv-canary: no attacher registered for pool class TpuFusedMHATokenToKVPool; supported: ['DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool', 'MHATokenToKVPool', 'MHATokenToKVPoolFP4', 'SWAKVPool']` |

The failure happens on both the prefill and the decode engine of a disaggregated pair, and would happen on a monolithic server the same way.
Nothing in argument validation rejects the flag on `--device tpu`, so the user gets a crash with `exited with -9` instead of a message.

**Expected behavior.** Either the canary works on TPU (an attacher that understands the fused 5-D layout), or `--kv-canary` other than `none`
is rejected at argument validation on TPU with a clear message. A configuration option must not take every rank down after the weights are loaded.

**1. The attacher registry knows only the generic pools and is keyed by exact type:**
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/kv_canary/pool_patcher/api.py#L26-L35
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/kv_canary/pool_patcher/api.py#L48-L55

`register_pool_attacher` exists but no TPU module calls it (no match for it outside `api.py`), so the TPU pool subclass is never registered.

**2. The TPU pool is a subclass with a fused layout.** `TpuFusedMHATokenToKVPool(MHATokenToKVPool)` builds one 5-D `kv_buffer` per layer for the
Pallas kernel instead of `k_buffer`/`v_buffer`:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/tpu/kv_pool.py#L71-L90

**3. The SWA adapter assumes the generic layout.** For `SWAKVPool` (gpt-oss) the adapter is found, but it reads `k_buffer[0]` and `v_buffer[0]`
of each sub-pool to size the canary buffers and to build the real-data row sources:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/kv_canary/pool_patcher/adapters/swa.py#L11-L80

**4. Tracebacks (identical on all 8 ranks of both engines):**

gpt-oss:
```
  File ".../sglang/srt/kv_canary/pool_patcher/api.py", line 58, in attach_canary_buffers
    groups = attacher(
  File ".../sglang/srt/kv_canary/pool_patcher/adapters/swa.py", line 22, in attach_swa
    full_group = _build_subpool_group(
  File ".../sglang/srt/kv_canary/pool_patcher/adapters/swa.py", line 65, in _build_subpool_group
    num_slots = int(sub_pool.k_buffer[0].shape[0])
AttributeError: 'TpuFusedMHATokenToKVPool' object has no attribute 'k_buffer'. Did you mean: 'kv_buffer'?
[2026-10-08 17:30:28] Received sigquit from a child process. It usually means the child failed.
RuntimeError: An engine or router exited with -9
```

Qwen3-VL:
```
NotImplementedError: kv-canary: no attacher registered for pool class TpuFusedMHATokenToKVPool;
supported: ['DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool', 'MHATokenToKVPool', 'MHATokenToKVPoolFP4', 'SWAKVPool']
```
## Fix proposal

1. **Short-term: Reject up front.** In server-argument validation, when `device == "tpu"` and `kv_canary != "none"`, raise a `ValueError` that names the flag and the reason, until an attacher exists. This is a two-line change and removes the start-up crash.
2. **Long-term: Support the fused layout.** Register `TpuFusedMHATokenToKVPool` with an attacher (via `register_pool_attacher` from the TPU hardware backend) that sizes the canary buffers from `kv_buffer[0].shape[0]` and builds the real-data row sources from the K and V halves of the fused row (the pool already exposes `get_fused_kv_buffer`). Make `_build_subpool_group` in the SWA adapter use the same accessor, so hybrid-SWA models on TPU work too.
3. **Fail softer.** An exception from `attach_canary_buffers` during pool set-up sh

### Reproduction

1. Start any model on TPU with `--kv-canary log` (one monolithic server is enough):
   `python -m sglang.launch_server --device tpu --model-path openai/gpt-oss-120b --tp-size 8 --kv-canary log --kv-canary-real-data partial`
2. Watch the log for about 10 s after `Load weight end`.

**Observed.** All ranks raise during `attach_canary_buffers`; the launcher reports `An engine or router exited with -9`.
**Expected.** The server starts with the canary active, or exits at argument parsing with "kv-canary is not supported on TPU".

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| sglang-torchtpu | `main` @ 09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709 (2026-10-07), sglang 0.5.13.dev7249 |
| TPU stack | torch-tpu 0.1.1+release.2026.9.22.20260927223741, libtpu 0.0.47, tpu-sync-torch 0.0.1.dev20261002213151, torch 2.11.0+cpu, transformers 5.8.1 |
| Hardware | Two TPU v7x hosts (4 chips / 8 TensorCores each), prefill on host a, decode on host b, TP 8, EP 8 |
| Flags that trigger it | `--kv-canary log --kv-canary-real-data partial --kv-canary-sweep-interval 50` on both engines (`--disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum` was also on; it is unrelated, see below) |
| Models | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (MXFP4, fp8 KV, page 64); `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct` (bf16, fp8 KV, page 128) |

title: [P0] [TPU/PD/Raiden] P/D handshake never completes on some pairs. Decode stays in Bootstrapping with no deadline, prefill holds the request in its inflight queue.
body:
### Checklist

- [ ] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [ ] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Summary
On three freshly started gpt-oss-120b 1P1D pairs with --max-running-requests 1 and 140k context, the very first request—and every subsequent one—stalls indefinitely without producing a token (whereas 2-slot, 8-slot, and 1M-context single-slot recipes serve normally). The prefill engine runs the 8k prompt chunk, places the request in its inflight queue, and idles; the decode engine's KV receiver stays in KVPoll.Bootstrapping for the entire 30-minute observation. Both engines report /health OK and log nothing until the client disconnects.

The stall never resolves because neither side enforces a deadline once stuck here:

- Decode (RaidenKVReceiver): The raiden receiver never checks SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT. Its only timeout (_check_waiting_timeout) starts init_time inside send_metadata, which runs after leaving Bootstrapping. 
- Prefill (RaidenKVSender): Advances straight to WaitingForInput and bounds the wait with fail_decode_silence(room, init_time, bootstrap_timeout)—which is set to 7200 s in this recipe and returns False (disabling the deadline) as soon as the decode asks for the room.

**Expected behavior:** Either the handshake completes and serves the request, or both engines time out within SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT—logging a clear error, releasing prefill KV pages, returning HTTP 500, and leaving the pair ready for the next request.

## Fix proposal (PLEASE DOUBLE CHECK ON YOUR OWN)
1. **Give the raiden receiver a bootstrap deadline.** In `RaidenKVReceiver.poll`, while the room status is `Bootstrapping`, apply `kv_mgr.bootstrap_timeout` from the receiver's creation time, as `_check_bootstrap_timeout` does for the other backends, and conclude the room as failed with a message naming the room and the elapsed time. This alone turns a 30-minute silent hold into a 300-second logged failure.
2. **Keep a prefill-side deadline until the transfer actually starts.** `fail_decode_silence` stops counting once the decode has asked; add a second bound from that moment until `maybe_start_pull` or the first chunk read, so a decode that asked and then stalled cannot pin the prefill's pages forever.
3. **Log the handshake.** At INFO level, log on both sides when a room is registered, when the decode's request is received, and when the reply is sent. 
4. Need further investigate about the tigger conditions.


### Reproduction

The stall is deterministic for one recipe and absent for every neighbouring recipe we ran. All pairs: gpt-oss-120b, raiden, radix cache off on
the prefill, both engines freshly started, first request sent within a minute of the load balancer becoming healthy.

| Pair | `--max-running-requests` (both engines) | `--context-length` / `--max-total-tokens` | `SGLANG_RAIDEN_HOST_POOL_GB` | Compile batch sizes | Requests | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F11_gpt-oss_A_128k_mr1 | 1 | 140,288 / 786,432 | 128 | [1] | 8k, 8k | **stall on the first request; the next stalls too** |
| F12_…_mr1_try1 (fresh pair) | 1 | 140,288 / 786,432 | 128 | [1] | 8k, 8k, 32k | **stall on every request** |
| F12_…_mr1_try2 (fresh pair) | 1 | 140,288 / 786,432 | 128 | [1] | 8k | **stall on the first request** |
| F11_gpt-oss_A_128k_mr2 | 2 | 140,288 / 786,432 | 128 | [1, 2] | 8k, 32k, 131k | served, 6 of 6 |
| Config A campaign (A_gptoss_128k_run1/run2) | 8 | 140,288 / 786,432 | 128 | [1, 2, 4, 8] | ~200 requests over two days | served |
| A_gptoss_1m_run1/run2 | 1 | 1,056,768 / 1,114,112 | 320 | [1] | 1k, 8k (longer prompts hit F-11) | served |
| F11_gpt-oss_A_1m_mr4 | 4 | 1,056,768 / 1,114,112 | 320 | [1, 2, 4] | 8k, 32k, 131k | served |


1. Start the pair with the "recipe that stalls" flags above (both engines freshly started).
2. Send one 8,192-token prompt with `max_new_tokens 64` through the load balancer.
3. After 60 s: decode `curl -s http://<decode>:30000/metrics | grep -E 'num_running|prealloc|transfer'`; prefill
   `curl -s http://<prefill>:30000/metrics | grep -E 'num_running|inflight'`.
4. `py-spy dump --pid <decode TP0 scheduler> --nonblocking`.

**Observed.** No answer. Prefill: one running request in the inflight queue. Decode: queues 0, scheduler in `_update_handshake_waiters`. Nothing is logged until the client disconnects.
**Expected.** An answer in seconds, or a failed request within 300 s with an error on both sides.



### Environment

|---|---|
| sglang-torchtpu | `main` @ 09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709 (2026-10-07), sglang 0.5.13.dev7249 |
| TPU stack | torch-tpu 0.1.1+release.2026.9.22.20260927223741, libtpu 0.0.47, tpu-sync-torch 0.0.1.dev20261002213151, torch 2.11.0+cpu, transformers 5.8.1 |
| Hardware | Two TPU v7x hosts (4 chips / 8 TensorCores each), prefill on host a, decode on host b, TP 8, EP 8 |

title: [P0] [TPU/PD] n>1 (parallel sampling) never returns through the P/D pair. Every sub-request of a prompt reuses the same bootstrap room, and the decode engine holds the leftover request until the client disconnects
body:
### Checklist

- [ ] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [ ] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Summary
A /generate request with parallel sampling "n": 2 through a 1P1D pair hangs indefinitely, while all other sampling cases finish in < 2s. Although normalize_batch_and_arguments expands the load balancer's single bootstrap_room integer into [room, room + 1], _handle_batch_request builds all three sub-requests (one max_new_tokens = 0 prefix request plus two sample requests) from prompt index obj[0]. As a result, all three sub-requests carry the exact same bootstrap_room = room and collide in transfer bookkeeping on both engines, leaving the decode engine holding the race loser with allocated prompt KV pages (128 tokens) and zero throughput until the client disconnects.

**Expected behavior:**

- Return two completions in a few seconds (as in monolithic mode), or reject n > 1 in disaggregated mode with HTTP 400 at validation.
- OR Never hold a request indefinitely with KV resources allocated.

## Code trace

**1. The load balancer attaches one room per HTTP request.** For a single prompt (no batch) the mini-LB adds a single integer `bootstrap_room`
(and host and port), regardless of `n`:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/sgl-model-gateway/bindings/python/src/sglang_router/mini_lb.py#L490-L513

**2. Normalization expands the room per sample.** With `parallel_sample_num = 2`, `num = batch_size × parallel_sample_num = 2`, and an integer
room becomes `[room, room + 1]`:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L583-L603
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L886-L910

**3. The expansion loop uses the prompt index, not the sample index.** `_handle_batch_request` takes `objs = [obj[i] for i in range(batch_size)]`
(here one object, carrying `bootstrap_room[0]`), sends a prefix request built from it with `max_new_tokens = 0`, then sends `parallel_sample_num`
copies of the same tokenized object with new rids but the same bootstrap fields:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py#L2003-L2060

So the prefill engine and the decode engine each see three requests with identical `bootstrap_room`. The room is the key of the per-request
transfer state on both sides (`register_decode_request`, `check_status`, `send_kv_chunk`), so two of the three registrations overwrite or wait on
the third.

**4. The prefix request has no business on the decode side.** Its purpose is to populate the prefix cache once so the samples reuse it. In
disaggregated mode it is still forwarded to both engines, allocates KV on the decode (`is_prefill_only` is true, nothing will be generated) and
then depends on a transfer whose room is shared with two other requests:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L1430-L1435

## Fix proposal

1. **One room per sub-request.** In `_handle_batch_request`, index the bootstrap fields by the sub-request number: the sample `k` of prompt `i` should use `bootstrap_room[i * parallel_sample_num + k]`, which `_normalize_bootstrap_params` already produces. The prefix request needs its own room as well (allocate `num + batch_size` rooms, or derive one from the prompt's room with an offset that cannot collide).
2. **Until fixed, validate.** Reject `n > 1` with HTTP 400 in disaggregated mode so clients get an immediate answer instead of a silent hold.


### Reproduction

1. Start a gpt-oss-120b pair (prefill + decode, raiden, mini-LB).
2. Send:
   ```
   curl -s -m 60 $LB/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"text":"The three primary colors are","sampling_params":{"temperature":0,"max_new_tokens":32,"n":2}}'
   ```
3. While it waits: `curl -s http://<decode>:30000/metrics | grep -E 'num_running_reqs|num_used_tokens'`.

**Observed.** Step 2 times out. Step 3 shows one running request with 128 used tokens and no progress; the prefill shows nothing running.
**Expected.** Two completions in a few seconds.

Control: the same request against a monolithic server returns two completions.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| sglang-torchtpu | `main` @ 09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709 (2026-10-07), sglang 0.5.13.dev7249 |
| TPU stack | torch-tpu 0.1.1+release.2026.9.22.20260927223741, libtpu 0.0.47, tpu-sync-torch 0.0.1.dev20261002213151, torch 2.11.0+cpu, transformers 5.8.1 |
| Hardware | Two TPU v7x hosts (4 chips / 8 TensorCores each), prefill on host a, decode on host b, TP 8, EP 8 |
| Model | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (MXFP4), KV cache fp8_e4m3, page size 64 |
| Topology | raiden transfer backend, Python mini load balancer (`sglang_router.mini_lb`) on port 8080, radix cache off on the prefill |

title: [P0] [TPU/Compile] One image above the precompiled ViT range kills the Qwen3-VL prefill engine.
body:
### Checklist

- [ ] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [ ] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Summary
A single /v1/chat/completions request with a 1920×1080 image (8,160 patches) crashes the Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B prefill engine. Because SGLANG_IMAGE_MAX_PIXELS defaults to ~12.8M pixels while SGLANG_TPU_VIT_MAX_PRECOMPILE_PATCHES defaults to 4,900, the image passes through unscaled and exceeds the precompiled ViT buckets. Instead of falling back to the saved uncompiled encoder (self.eager_fn) like MoonVitTpuCompilePolicy and Gemma4VisionTpuCompilePolicy do, ViTTpuCompileRunner unconditionally calls compiled_fn. Since warmup freezes torch.compile with set_stance("fail_on_recompile"), this raises an uncaught RuntimeError that kills all prefill scheduler ranks.

**Expected behavior.** 
- Run oversized images eagerly via self.eager_fn (matching MoonViT and Gemma4), or reject them at validation with HTTP 400/413.
- Never allow a per-request failure to crash the scheduler event loop.

## Fix proposal (Please Double Check On Your Own)

1. **Port the eager fallback to the generic ViT runner.** In `VisionTpuCompilePolicy.run` (or in `Qwen3VLVisionTpuCompilePolicy._install_run_adapter`), when `bucket_for_patches(total)` returns an unbucketed count and `self.eager_fn` is set, call `eager_fn` under `torch.no_grad()` exactly as `MoonVitTpuCompilePolicy._run_one` and `Gemma4VisionTpuCompilePolicy` do, and change the warning to "running this image eagerly". This is the minimal fix and it matches the behavior the other two policies already ship.
2. **Reject what cannot be served.** If eager execution is not wanted for a deployment, validate at request time: compute the patch count from `grid_thw` in the processor and return HTTP 413 with the maximum supported pixels when it exceeds the top bucket. 
3. **Catch the failure and abort the request** A `RuntimeError` from the multimodal encoder for one request should fail that request, not the scheduler.




### Reproduction

1. Start Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct on TPU with `--enable-torch-compile` and no `max_pixels` cap (one monolithic server is enough).
2. Wait for `Warmup complete; froze torch.compile via set_stance('fail_on_recompile')` in the log.
3. Send one chat request with one 1920 × 1080 image, for example:
   `python scripts/mm_request.py --url $SERVER --model qwen3-vl-30b --num-images 1 --resolution 1920x1080 --max-tokens 48 --temperature 0`
   (any PNG of that size as a `data:` URL in `/v1/chat/completions` behaves the same).
4. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' $SERVER/health`.

**Observed.** Step 3 returns HTTP 500 after about 65 s. Step 4 returns `000`. The log shows the `ViTTpuCompileRunner: patch count 8160 exceeds
the largest precompiled bucket 4900` warning followed by `RuntimeError: Detected recompile when torch.compile stance is 'fail_on_recompile'`
on every rank.
**Expected.** HTTP 200 with a slower first token (eager encoder), or HTTP 400/413; the server stays healthy either way.

Controls: the same request with `--mm-process-config '{"image":{"max_pixels":313600}}'` should downscale the image and succeed; with
`SGLANG_TPU_VIT_MAX_PRECOMPILE_PATCHES=8192` the image should land in a precompiled bucket and succeed.

title: [P0] [TPU/PD/Raiden] Client disconnect during chunked prefill kills the prefill engine - aborted request's KV row is released twice
body:
### Checklist

- [ ] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [ ] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Summary
A client opens a streaming request with a long prompt (131k tokens) against a 1-prefill + 1-decode pair and closes the connection two seconds later, while the prefill engine is still processing the prompt in chunks. Within a few seconds all eight prefill scheduler ranks exit with the same assertion, the launcher kills the process group, the load balancer goes down with it, and every in-flight and later request fails. 
The cause is a double release of the aborted request's KV row. The chunked-abort path defers the page release because the raiden transfer backend needs its outstanding transfer group to drain first. But the result of the chunk that was already in flight lands one step later and takes the regular aborted-result path, which frees the row immediately. When the deferred path later runs, the row is already gone, and the general release routine treats "release without a row" as legal only for Mamba-style caches. The configuration uses the plain chunk cache (radix cache off), so the assertion fires inside the scheduler loop and the process exits.

**Expected behavior.** A disconnect ends one request and nothing else:

1. The request's KV pages, request slot, metadata buffer and transfer room are released **exactly once**, after the raiden transfer group has drained, so no remote read is still touching the pages when they are reused.
2. Every other request is unaffected: queued requests, requests in flight on the decode side, and the client's next request all proceed normally.
3. Both engines stay healthy and the load balancer stays up; running requests and token usage return to their pre-request values within a bounded time (our test uses 60 s), and a follow-up request succeeds.
5. The event is logged at info level. If the abort bookkeeping fails for any reason, that one request is marked failed and the traceback is logged; the exception never escapes the scheduler loop.

## Code trace

**1. The disconnect becomes an abort for the request that is currently being chunked.** :
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L5765-L5768

**2. Next scheduling step: the pending abort is processed and the page release is deferred.** `process_pending_chunked_abort` marks the request aborted, calls `disagg_kv_sender.abort()`, and because the raiden sender declares `group_failure_requires_drain = True` and is not yet drained, it sets `defer_page_release`, drops the cache-side state, and appends the request to `_deferred_chunked_sender_aborts` instead of freeing its pages. It then clears `chunked_req`, so no further chunk is launched:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L3720-L3777
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/sender.py#L973

**3. The in-flight chunk's result lands and frees the row anyway.**  For an aborted request it calls `_retire_aborted_prefill_result`:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py#L905-L930

That routine checks `req.kv.holds_kv`, which is still true because step 2 deferred the release, and therefore releases the KV row immediately.
It does not consult the sender's drain state and does not know the request is on the deferred list:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py#L1198-L1222

After this, `req.kv.req_pool_idx` is `None` and `holds_kv` is false:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L969-L970

**4. The deferred path runs and releases the row a second time.** At the top of a later step, `get_next_disagg_prefill_batch_to_run` calls `process_pending_chunked_abort`, which first drains the deferred list. The sender reports drained, and the code calls `release_kv_cache` with no `holds_kv` guard:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py#L672
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L3779-L3796

**5. The release routine asserts.** `release_kv_cache` allows a release without a row only for a Mamba-capable cache. `SWAChunkCache` is not one, so it raises:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py#L292-L300

```
[TPx] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py", line 757, in event_loop_overlap_disagg_prefill
  File ".../sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py", line 672, in get_next_disagg_prefill_batch_to_run
    self.process_pending_chunked_abort()
  File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3734, in process_pending_chunked_abort
    self._drain_deferred_chunked_sender_aborts()
  File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3795, in _drain_deferred_chunked_sender_aborts
    release_kv_cache(req, self.tree_cache, is_insert=False)
  File ".../sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py", line 298, in release_kv_cache
    assert tree_cache.supports_mamba(), (
AssertionError: Only a mamba-capable tree cache allows freeing before alloc
```

**Another concern.** Step 3 frees the pages while the raiden group may still be draining, which is exactly what the deferral in step 2 was meant to prevent. On this run the sender had drained before step 4, so the crash is the only symptom we saw, but a slow drain could let the pages be reused while a remote read is still in progress.


## Fix proposal

1. **Make the deferred list the single owner of the release.**
2. **Guard the drain.** In `_drain_deferred_chunked_sender_aborts`, release only `if req.kv.holds_kv or req.kv.holds_mamba`, matching the guard that `_retire_aborted_prefill_result` and `release_aborted_prefill_waiting_req` already use. 
3. **Contain the blast radius.** A failure in the abort bookkeeping of one request should fail that request, not the scheduler. Wrapping the deferred-abort drain so that an exception marks the request failed and logs the traceback would keep the engine up even if another ordering bug of this kind exists.

A regression test: chunked prefill of a multi-chunk prompt on a `ChunkCache`, abort between chunks with a sender whose `drained()` returns false for one step, and assert that `release_kv_cache` is called exactly once for the request.


### Reproduction

1. Start a gpt-oss-120b pair as in the environment table (prefill with `--disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 8192`, raiden transfer).
2. Build a prompt of about 131k tokens (any text; needle content is irrelevant).
3. Open a streaming request and close the socket 2 s later. With Python `requests`:
   ```python
   import requests, socket, time
   r = requests.post(LB + "/generate", json={"text": PROMPT, "stream": True,
       "sampling_params": {"temperature": 0, "max_new_tokens": 1024, "ignore_eos": True}}, stream=True)
   time.sleep(2)
   s = r.raw._connection.sock; s.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR); s.close(); r.close()
   ```
   or: `python scripts/abort_test.py --url $LB --prompt-file prompts/gpt-oss/131072.jsonl --phase prefill --abort-after 2 --repeat 1`.
4. Wait 15 s. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' $PREFILL/health`.
5. `grep -A12 'Scheduler hit an exception' <prefill log> | head -20`.



### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| sglang-torchtpu | `main` @ 09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709 (2026-10-07), sglang 0.5.13.dev7249 |
| TPU stack | torch-tpu 0.1.1+release.2026.9.22.20260927223741, libtpu 0.0.47, tpu-sync-torch 0.0.1.dev20261002213151, torch 2.11.0+cpu, transformers 5.8.1 |
| Hardware | Two TPU v7x hosts (4 chips / 8 TensorCores each). Host a: prefill engine. Host b: decode engine. TP 8, EP 8 on each |
| Model | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (MXFP4 weights), KV cache fp8_e4m3, page size 64 |
| Prefill flags that matter | `--disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-transfer-backend raiden --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --context-length 140288` (overlap scheduling on; tree cache is `SWAChunkCache`) |

title: [P0] [TPU/PD] Chunked prefill deadlocks when the SWA continuation budget reaches 0 before window eviction runs (hit by gpt-oss-120b with --max-running-requests 1)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Summary

In disaggregated prefill with the radix cache off and `--max-running-requests 1`, gpt-oss-120b never finishes a prompt longer than 16,384 tokens. The prefill engine runs two chunks (8,192 and 8,000 tokens), then schedules nothing more. The request stays in the running slot until the client disconnects. Both engines report healthy and no watchdog fires, because no forward pass is in flight.

The cause is a chain of three things:

1. The sliding-window (SWA) KV pool is sized from a worst-case cap of two prefill chunks plus a small per-slot allowance plus one page. With one slot that is 16,832 tokens.
2. A TPU-only rule rounds the SWA pool **down** to a multiple of 8 pages (512 tokens): 16,832 becomes 16,384, exactly two chunks. The headroom the cap reserved is gone.
3. A continuation chunk is admitted only if `window + page` (192 tokens) stays free, and SWA pages that slid out of the window are freed only as a side effect of running the request's next chunk. After two chunks only 192 tokens are free, the third chunk is sized to 0 and is never scheduled, so the eviction that would free about 16,000 pages never runs.

With two or more request slots the rounding leaves at least 512 tokens of headroom, a small third chunk is admitted, it triggers the eviction and the pool cycles normally. So the failure is specific to one slot, which is exactly what a 1M-context recipe uses.

| `--max-running-requests` | SWA pool from the cap | After TPU rounding | Headroom above two chunks | Observed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16,832 | 16,384 | 0 | hang on every prompt > 16,384 tokens (4 of 4) |
| 4 | 17,984 | 17,920 | 1,536 | 8k, 32k, 131k prompts complete in 7 to 13 s (6 of 6) |
| 8 | 19,520 | 19,456 | 3,072 | 128k prompts complete; pool cycles 0.58 to 0.84 |

## Code trace

All links at commit 09d1244c26.

**1. Pool sizing.** `SWAChunkCapPoolConfigurator` is selected when the radix cache is off, `max_running_requests` is explicit and the model has a sliding window. It sizes the SWA pool from `compute_swa_request_cap`:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/pool_configurator.py#L1053-L1086

The cap for a prefill engine is `per_request * slots + chunks_in_flight * chunked_prefill_size + page_size`, where
`per_request = window + eviction_interval * draft_tokens + page_size + page_size` = 128 + 128 + 64 + 64 = 384, and `chunks_in_flight` is 2 with overlap scheduling:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/pool_configurator.py#L1007-L1050
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/pool_configurator.py#L679-L684

For one slot: 384 + 2 × 8192 + 64 = **16,832**. For four: 17,984. For eight: 19,520. The server log confirms each value.

**2. TPU rounding.** The pool is then rounded down to a multiple of 8 pages for the compiled decode kernel:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py#L517-L545

Log line on the prefill engine with one slot:
```
[hybrid-SWA] aligning swa_max_total_num_tokens 16832 -> 16384 (SWA page count must be a multiple of 8 for correct torch.compile decode on TPU)
```
16,384 is exactly `2 × chunked_prefill_size`. The 448 tokens of headroom the cap added are removed.

**3. Continuation chunk budget.** For a chunked request the next chunk is capped at `remaining_swa - (window + page)`, floored to a page:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/prefill_budget.py#L220-L227
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/prefill_budget.py#L278-L288

Chunk 1: 8,192 (pool empty, no cap). Chunk 2: remaining 8,192 − 192 = **8,000** (matches the log). After chunk 2,
16,192 tokens are in use and 192 are free. Chunk 3: cap = 192 − 192 = 0, `fit_chunk` returns `None`, and `add_chunked_req` returns the request without scheduling it:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_policy.py#L1157-L1200
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L4164-L4172

**4. Eviction only runs with a batch.** SWA pages outside the window are freed in `maybe_evict_swa`, which runs while a batch that contains the request is prepared. For a chunked request under overlap scheduling the first eviction happens on the third chunk
(`extend_batch_idx < 2` is skipped):
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L3895-L3960

No chunk is scheduled, so no eviction runs; no eviction runs, so no chunk can be scheduled. The scheduler loop idles with one running request.

**Why the monolithic server is fine.** With the radix cache on, the pool is sized by `swa_full_tokens_ratio`, which gives a far larger pool.
The monolithic 1M-context server served the same 256k, 512k and 1M prompts in our tests.

## How we detected it

We run a 1-prefill + 1-decode validation campaign on two TPU v7x hosts. The long-context sweep sends 32k, 128k, 256k and 1M prompts through the mini load balancer with a 1,800 s client timeout and a watchdog that polls both engines' `/metrics` every few seconds.

- The 32k request produced no output for 30 minutes. The watchdog showed, on the prefill engine, `num_running_reqs 1`,
  `num_used_tokens 16192`, `full_token_usage 0.01` and **`swa_token_usage 0.99`**, with `max_total_num_tokens_swa 16384`. The decode engine was idle.
- The prefill log showed two `Prefill batch` lines for the request, `#new-token: 8192` then `#new-token: 8000`, and nothing afterwards. When the client aborted, usage dropped to 0 and the same two lines repeated for the next request.
- The same recipe with `--max-running-requests 4` served 8k, 32k and 131k prompts in 7 to 13 s, and the SWA usage cycled between 0.54 and 0.91 as chunks were admitted and windows were evicted.
- The three pool sizes in the log (16,384 / 17,920 / 19,456) and the chunk sizes (8,192 / 8,000 / 1,344) match the formulas in the code trace exactly, which is how we located the mechanism.

The defect is that the continuation budget can reach 0 before the eviction that would raise it runs, and nothing else triggers that eviction. Fix 1 removes the defect for every pool size. Fix 2 keeps this configuration away from the edge. Fix 3 turns a silent hang into an error.

## Fix proposal

The defect is that the continuation budget can reach 0 before the eviction that would raise it runs, and nothing else triggers that eviction. Three options to be considered: 
1.  removes the defect for every pool size. 2. keeps this configuration away from the edge. 3. turns a silent hang into an error.

### Reproduction

Two hosts, prefill on a, decode on b, raiden transfer. Only the prefill flags matter for the hang; the decode can use the same recipe.

1. Start the prefill engine with: `--disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-transfer-backend raiden --disable-radix-cache
   --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-running-requests 1 --context-length 1056768 --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
   --attention-backend pallas_tpu_rpa_v3 --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --enable-torch-compile` on `openai/gpt-oss-120b`.
2. Confirm the pool size: `grep 'aligning swa_max_total_num_tokens' <prefill log>` prints `16832 -> 16384`.
3. Start the decode engine and the load balancer, then send one 32,768-token prompt with `max_new_tokens 64`.
4. After 60 s: `curl -s http://<prefill>:30000/metrics | grep -E 'swa_token_usage|num_running_reqs'`.
5. `grep 'Prefill batch' <prefill log> | tail -3`.

**Observed.** Step 3 never returns. Step 4 shows `swa_token_usage 0.99`, `num_running_reqs 1`. Step 5 shows `#new-token: 8192`, then `8000`,
then nothing. An 8k prompt (one chunk) completes normally.
**Expected.** The 32k prompt completes in a few seconds, as it does with `--max-running-requests 4`, or the request fails with an error.

Control: repeat with `--max-running-requests 2`. The pool becomes 17,216 → 16,896 after rounding, 512 tokens of headroom, and the hang does not occur.


### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| sglang-torchtpu | `main` @ 09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709 (2026-10-07), sglang 0.5.13.dev7249 |
| TPU stack | torch-tpu 0.1.1+release.2026.9.22.20260927223741, libtpu 0.0.47, tpu-sync-torch 0.0.1.dev20261002213151, torch 2.11.0+cpu, transformers 5.8.1 |
| Hardware | Two TPU v7x hosts (4 chips / 8 TensorCores each). Host a: prefill engine. Host b: decode engine. TP 8, EP 8 on each |
| Model | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` (MXFP4 weights, `sliding_window` 128), KV cache fp8_e4m3, page size 64 |
| Prefill flags that matter | `--disaggregation-mode prefill --disaggregation-transfer-backend raiden --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-running-requests 1 --context-length 1056768 --enable-torch-compile` (overlap scheduling on) |

title: [TPU] PCP with the fused MoE's SparseCore kernels halts or returns wrong tokens on libtpu >= 0.0.46
body:
With PCP (`--enable-prefill-cp --attn-cp-size 8`) and a MoE model that runs the fused MoE's SparseCore kernels (`SGLANG_TPU_FUSED_MOE_SC_GATHER=1`, the default), libtpu 0.0.46 and newer either halt a SparseCore or return NaN / garbage tokens. Bisecting released libtpu on the same setup: 0.0.45 is correct; 0.0.46, 0.0.46.1, 0.0.46.2, 0.0.47 and 0.0.49 are affected. main pins 0.0.47.

Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8, fp8 KV, PCP8 on one 8-core host:

| Setup | libtpu 0.0.49 | libtpu 0.0.49 + flag below |
|---|---|---|
| PCP8 + EP8, SparseCore offloads off | SparseCore halt during warmup | no halt; GSM8K 94.3%, needle prompts 16/16 |
| PCP8 + EP8, default libtpu flags | NaN on ~5K-token prompts | correct |
| PCP8 + MoE-DP8, SparseCore offloads off | GSM8K 0%, needle prompts 0/16 | GSM8K 94.4%, needle prompts 16/16 |

- SparseCore offloads off: `--xla_tpu_enable_sparse_core_collective_offload_{all_reduce,all_gather,reduce_scatter}=false --xla_tpu_offload_gather_to_sparsecore=false`.
- Needle prompts: 16 concurrent prompts of 0.8-2.3K tokens, each asking for a code word hidden in it.
- TP8 + EP8 without PCP is correct (GSM8K 94.6%).

**Workaround:** add `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_enable_fast_merge_fallback=false` to `LIBTPU_INIT_ARGS`. It fixes every row above, with no measurable change in compile time or prefill throughput.

**Why CI does not catch it:** no TPU CI or nightly test runs PCP; the TPU MoE tests run TP / EP / DP without PCP.

**Related:** #1065 (FP8 fused reduce-scatter MoE kernel, TP / EP without PCP) regressed in the same libtpu release. Whether this flag also fixes it is untested.

**To close:**
- Set the flag under PCP until a fixed libtpu is pinned, and allow `--ep-size` with PCP again (#662 currently refuses it).
- Add a PCP + MoE accuracy test (GSM8K and mixed 1-5K-token prompts) to the nightly suite.
- Drop the flag once the pinned libtpu is fixed.

- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.

### Describe the bug

## Summary

With `--enable-torch-compile`, only the vision encoder of `Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct` is compiled. The MoE language model runs in eager mode for every decode step. Decode speed is about 6 tokens/s for one request (about 160 ms per step). On the same hosts and software stack, gpt-oss-120b decodes at 176 tokens/s (5.7 ms per step), although it activates more parameters per token.

## Cause
The cause is a missing registration. `[qwen3_vl.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py)` attaches the decoder compile policy only to the dense language model class. The MoE class used by the 30B-A3B model has no policy. Because the vision policy was installed, the graph runner treats the model as handled and skips its whole-model fallback, so the decoder never compiles. Nothing in the log warns about this. 

## How we detected it

1. We ran monolithic servers for gpt-oss-120b and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B with identical flags (`--enable-torch-compile`, TP 8, EP 8) as golden references for a prefill/decode disaggregation test campaign.
2. Text-only requests with 1,024 new tokens took 7 to 13 s on gpt-oss and 160 to 195 s on Qwen3-VL. For a model that activates about 3B parameters per token (Qwen) against about 5B (gpt-oss), the Qwen result is about 25 times too slow for the hardware.
3. The Qwen server log contains only one compile policy line, for the vision tower, and no decoder policy:
   ```
   [TP0 EP0] VisionTpuCompilePolicy: installed qwen3_vl_vit_encoder on ViTTpuCompileRunner.forward.
   [TP0 EP0] VisionTpuCompilePolicy.precompile: warming 29 patch counts [196, 256, ..., 3364]
   [TP0 EP0] [TPU] TpuGraphRunner precompile done
   ```
   The gpt-oss log shows the whole-model fallback instead (`declares no TPU compile policies; falling back to DecoderTpuCompilePolicy`).
4. Every `Decode batch` line for Qwen reports `gen throughput (token/s): 6` to `13` (two requests) and the step time matches eager dispatch overhead, not compute. Outputs are correct (token-identical to a second server, needles retrieved), so this is a performance defect.


## Code Trace

- Dense Qwen3-VL language model gets the decoder policy:
  https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1380-L1388
- The MoE variant defines `Qwen3MoeLLMModel` and selects it as `language_model_cls`, with no `support_torch_compile` call anywhere in the file:
  https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl_moe.py#L43
  https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl_moe.py#L204-L210
- The graph runner applies the whole-model fallback only when **no** policy was installed. The vision policy installs, so the fallback is skipped:
  https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/tpu_graph_runner.py#L274-L295
- The same `Qwen3VLDecoderTpuCompilePolicy` already serves a MoE decoder (Qwen3.5), so it is suitable for `Qwen3MoeLLMModel`:
  https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L2377-L2380
  https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/09d1244c2641c3232ec0fcf5dd2d3bd372d5d709/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/tpu/compilation/decoder_compile_policy.py#L1473

### Reproduction

## How to reproduce

1. Start the server (one TPU v7x host):
   ```
   python -m sglang.launch_server --device tpu --dtype bfloat16 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \
     --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct --served-model-name qwen3-vl-30b \
     --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 --attention-backend pallas_tpu_rpa_v3 --page-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
     --context-length 140288 --max-total-tokens 786432 --max-running-requests 4 \
     --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 8192 --tpu-compile-tokens 512 1024 2048 4096 8192 --tpu-compile-bs 1 2 4 \
     --enable-torch-compile --torch-compile-max-bs 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.5 --sampling-backend pytorch \
     --skip-server-warmup --enable-metrics --grammar-backend none
   ```
2. Wait for `The server is fired up and ready to roll!`.
3. Send one text request:
   ```
   curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/generate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"text":"Write a long story about a lighthouse keeper.","sampling_params":{"temperature":0,"max_new_tokens":1024,"ignore_eos":true}}'
   ```
4. Read the server log.

title: [TPU/PD/MiniLB] Prefill counts aborts and transfer failures for streaming requests that succeeded
body:
### Issue

**The problem sits in the MiniLB (`sglang_router/mini_lb.py`). It shows in the prefill's metrics and logs.**

For a streaming request the MiniLB closes the prefill's connection as soon as the decode has finished answering. Under load the prefill has not wrapped up its own side yet, so it sees a client disconnect and counts the request as aborted, although it succeeded.

- In a 4-hour 2P2D stress run, 8% of all requests (4,966 of 60,380) were counted in the prefill's `sglang:num_aborted_requests_total`, and 88 in `sglang:num_transfer_failed_reqs_total`. Almost none were real.
- No request is affected. Only the prefill's counters and logs are wrong, which makes its abort and transfer-failure panels unreliable.
- The Rust gateway does not do this.

Where in the code: `MiniLoadBalancer.generate_stream` in `sgl-model-gateway/bindings/python/src/sglang_router/mini_lb.py`. Its inner generator `stream_results()` reads only the decode response, and its `finally: await close_upstreams()` closes the prefill response as soon as the decode stream ends. On the prefill, `TokenizerManager.create_abort_task` then aborts the request 2 s after the disconnect. If the request is still in the prefill's transfer queue, `disaggregation/prefill.py` also logs `Prefill transfer failed ... Aborted by AbortReq` and counts a failed transfer.

Expected: a request that completed is not counted as aborted or failed on the prefill.

title: [TPU/PD/MiniLB] A decode that dies mid-stream ends the client's stream silently
body:
### Issue

**The problem sits in the MiniLB (`sglang_router/mini_lb.py`).**

When a decode worker dies while it is streaming answers, the MiniLB does not tell the client. The stream just stops, with HTTP 200, no error and no `[DONE]`. An answer that was cut off looks like a complete one.

- Seen on 55 open streams when a decode was lost during a 2P2D stress run (the cluster preempted its pod).
- The MiniLB logs an unhandled exception with a long traceback for each stream.

Where in the code: `MiniLoadBalancer.generate_stream` in `sgl-model-gateway/bindings/python/src/sglang_router/mini_lb.py`. Its inner generator `stream_results()` forwards `decode_response.content` to the client. When the decode's connection breaks, aiohttp raises `ClientPayloadError` inside that loop. Nothing catches it, so it escapes after the 200 status has already been sent.

Expected: the client gets an explicit error, and the MiniLB logs one line.

title: P0 [TPU/PD/Raiden] Prefill holds a request for the full transfer timeout (120 s) after the decode gives up
body:
### Issue

**This involves both tpu-raiden and sglang-torchtpu.**

In P/D with the raiden transfer backend, when the decode gives a request up after the prefill has registered its KV for reading, the prefill keeps that registration until raiden expires it (`SGLANG_RAIDEN_TIMEOUT_S`, 120 s by default). For that time the prefill keeps the request's KV pages, a running-request slot and its HTTP reply.

Symptom, in a 12-minute run with injected failures: for 3 of the first 9 failed requests the decode answered in under 5 s and the prefill answered 120 to 125 s later.

Cause: `disaggregation/raiden/sender.py`. The sender withholds its failure while one of the room's reads is still registered, and raiden has no call to cancel a registered send. So the room stays until the registration expires.

Impact:

- A client behind a load balancer that waits for both replies waits 120 s.
- Prefill capacity (KV pages and a request slot) is held for 120 s per affected request.

Expected: the prefill releases the room and answers within seconds of the decode giving up.

### Reproduction

How we hit it: injected failures on the decode side of the transfer during the fault injection runs, with the prefill's reply time recorded separately from the decode's.

1. Start 1 prefill and 1 decode server for GPT-OSS-120B with `--disaggregation-transfer-backend raiden`.
2. Inject a failure on the decode side of the transfer, for example `fail` at `kv_cache_manager.api.start_read` or `transfer_recv_session.h2d.complete`.
3. Send long-prompt requests and record the reply time of the prefill separately from the reply time of the decode.

title: P0 [TPU/PD/Raiden] Decode waits the full transfer timeout (120 s) when the prefill fails a transfer
body:
### Issue

**This involves both tpu-raiden and sglang-torchtpu.**

In P/D with the raiden transfer backend, when the prefill side of a KV transfer fails (the device-to-host copy, the push, or the read registration), the decode is not told. It keeps the request, its KV pages and its host staging memory until the read's own deadline (`SGLANG_RAIDEN_TIMEOUT_S`, 120 s by default), and only then returns an error to the client.

Symptom:

- The prefill logged `failed={'swa:<room>'}` and answered HTTP 500 at 07:06:37. The decode answered HTTP 500 at 07:08:37, exactly 120 s later.
- In a 12-minute run with injected failures, failed requests took 10 s at the median and 123 s at the maximum.

Cause: a failure on the prefill side never reaches the decode's receive session. No data arrives and no error arrives. sglang has no message that tells the decode, and raiden has no call to cancel a read. sglang rightly does not free a room while raiden still holds one of its reads, because freeing the pages under a running transfer would corrupt their next owner. So the room stays until raiden's deadline.

Impact:

- The client waits up to 120 s for an error that is already known.
- The decode holds KV pages, a request slot and host staging memory for that time, which lowers capacity exactly during an incident.

Expected: the decode returns its error within seconds of the prefill's failure.

### Reproduction

How we hit it: injected failures on the prefill side of the transfer during the fault injection runs.

1. Start 1 prefill and 1 decode server for GPT-OSS-120B with `--disaggregation-transfer-backend raiden`.
2. Inject a failure on the prefill side of the transfer, for example `fail` at `raiden_manager_base.h2h.write` or `transfer_send_session.d2h.complete`.
3. Send long-prompt requests and compare the time of the prefill's error reply with the time of the decode's error reply.

title: [TPU/PD/Raiden] A failed transfer sets off a reconnect and error-log storm in raiden
body:
### Issue

**This is a raiden issue. The fix belongs in tpu-raiden. It is filed here because it affects P/D serving in sglang-torchtpu.**

When a KV transfer ends early on the decode (a failure or a timeout), the prefill still has the pushes for all remaining layers in flight. The decode rejects each late push by returning an error, which closes the socket. The prefill cannot return that connection to its pool, so it opens a new one for the next push. One failed transfer costs dozens of connections and error lines on both servers.

Symptom, in a 12-minute run with 22 failed transfers:

- Decode: 687 x `Incoming push rejected ... NOT_FOUND: No active receive session` and 687 x `ProcessPeerRequest failed`
- Prefill: 214 x `H2hWrite failed ...: Explicit push destination handshake failed`
- `conn_pool.borrow.connect` ran 262 times, against 0 in a 1-hour run with no failures.
- About 64 error lines per failed request on the decode and about 10 on the prefill.

Cause, in tpu-raiden (`transport/block_transport.cc`, `transport/lib/socket_transport_adapter.cc`, `core/transfer_send_session.cc`): the send session queues every layer's push without waiting for the previous one. When the read ends on the decode, the remaining pushes are already on their way. The decode answers each one with an error and closes the socket. The prefill sees EOF during the handshake, cannot pool the connection, and reconnects.

Impact:

- The log flood hides the first error, which is the one that matters.
- The reconnects add load exactly when something is already failing. On a slow network each reconnect can stall as well.
- No wrong data.

Expected: one failed transfer produces one clear error and does not cost extra connections.

### Reproduction

How we hit it: any transfer that failed in the middle of a multi-layer transfer during the fault injection runs.

1. Start 1 prefill and 1 decode server for GPT-OSS-120B with `--disaggregation-transfer-backend raiden`.
2. Make a transfer fail in the middle. With fault injection: `fail` at `block_transport.recv.payload` on the decode, or a delay of more than 10 s at a control-plane hook.
3. Send long-prompt requests and count the error lines and new connections per failed request.

title: [TPU/Compile] Speed up precompile
body:
Precompile is the largest part of TPU server bring-up and takes minutes on
larger models. Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B cold-starts in 370-388 s on one v7x host,
almost all of it in the ViT precompile (29 patch-count buckets).

Every rank traces the same programs independently, and tracing is sequential
per rank. This slows restarts, scale-out, and model development.

title: [TPU/PP] Support independent stage execution for Pipeline Parallelism (PP×PCP / PP×TP)
body:
## What Is Not Working

Pipeline Parallelism with in-stage parallelism (`PP×PCP` in #827 and `PP×TP` in #869) partitions a TPU slice into disjoint stage process groups. Because different pipeline stages hold different layers (e.g. stage 0 has the embedding, the last stage has the LM head, and middle stages have only decoder layers), stages execute different stage-local workloads before meeting at cross-stage communication (`ppermute`).

On current `torch_tpu` (`main`), this hits three issues:

1. **Host hang on asymmetric stages:** When one pipeline stage runs a different number of stage-local collectives than other stages (during warmup, profiling, or steady-state decode), execution hangs waiting across stages.
2. **Decode latency regression with framework-side padding (#1004):** Padding stage launches on the SGLang side avoids the hang on GPT-OSS-120B `PP4×PCP2`, but decode ITL regresses by **36–41%** (`38.7 ms` vs `28.4 ms` at 4096/64 `c=4`, and `45.3 ms` vs `32.1 ms` at 2048/128 `c=8` on v7x).
3. **Stage-scoped Pallas meshes:** Creating a Pallas mesh for a stage process group (`size < world_size`) raises `ValueError: torch_tpu pallas kernels currently require full world-size meshes only`.

---

## What Is Required from `torch_tpu`

1. **Independent stage execution:** Disjoint pipeline stage groups must be able to execute different numbers of stage-local collectives/programs without hanging or requiring framework-side dummy launches, and then synchronize at world-group collectives.
2. **No cross-stage performance penalty:** Stage-local execution under `PP×PCP` / `PP×TP` should match the pre-regression decode latency (~`28.5 ms` median ITL at 4096/64 `c=4` on GPT-OSS-120B `PP4×PCP2`).
3. **Compilation cache support for all stages:** Persistent compilation caches (AOTAutograd and Tier-2/3) must distinguish process groups with different member ranks and work across all pipeline stages without warm-start recompilation.
4. **Stage-scoped Pallas meshes:** Support `get_pallas_mesh(process_group=stage_group)` for kernels that operate within a pipeline stage.

---

## Tracking Links

- **SGLang PRs:** #827 (`PP×PCP`), #869 (`PP×TP`), #973 (guard tests & reproducer), #1004 (temporary SGLang-side workaround)
- **`torch_tpu` PRs:** [google-pytorch/torch_tpu#4777](https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu/pull/4777), [google-pytorch/torch_tpu#4387](https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu/pull/4387)

title: [TPU/Raiden] Refuse unsupported configs up front: dst_tp > src_tp, MLA under push-reshard, hybrid-linear (Mamba) pools
body:
The raiden README lists configurations it does not support: MLA, Mamba/NSA, and `dst_tp > src_tp` ([README L87-90](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/README.md#L87-L90)). None of them is refused. Each one fails later, slowly or with an unhelpful error. As far as I can tell from the code, none of them corrupts output. The request is a startup or bootstrap-time refusal that names the unsupported combination.

Code refs are permalinks at `c6067bab13`. `disaggregation/raiden/` and `disaggregation/common/conn.py` are unchanged through `49959c5cf` (current `main`).

## Cases

| Config | What happens today | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Decode attn TP > prefill attn TP | The generic bootstrap only emits a "Performance is NOT guaranteed" warning and routes to the pull path. The prefill keeps one `decode_addr` per room and replies once, but several decode ranks are waiting on that room. Every request fails: immediately when the head split changes page bytes (e.g. bf16), otherwise after the 300 s waiting timeout. Decode polls are MIN-reduced across ranks, so no partially transferred request is served | [common/conn.py L1022-1032](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/common/conn.py#L1022-L1032), [sender.py L53-70](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/sender.py#L53-L70), [sender.py L403-423](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/sender.py#L403-L423) |
| MLA with asymmetric attn TP (push-reshard) | The MLA pool tensor is 4-D, so `head_pair_bytes` raises `IndexError` on `shape[4]`. The listener swallows it (see #1078) and each request stalls for 300 s | [conn.py L303-304](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/conn.py#L303-L304) |
| Hybrid-linear (Mamba-style) pools | `HybridLinearKVPool` never runs `KVCache.__init__`, so it has no `layer_num`. `get_raiden_kv_caches` raises `AttributeError` at manager setup and the server fails to start, with no hint that raiden P/D doesn't support this model | [memory_pool.py L3962-3970](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py#L3962-L3970), [raiden/common.py L80-85](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/common.py#L80-L85) |

## Suggested fix

- **At bootstrap,** both TP sizes are known. Refuse `dst_attn_tp > src_attn_tp` for the raiden backend with a message, and fail the request rather than raising, because a `RuntimeError` there takes down the decode scheduler.
- **At raiden manager init,** refuse MLA under push-reshard, and refuse pools without the fused 5-D KV layout (hybrid-linear), with an explicit message.
- **README:** the same list still says "speculative draft KV" is not covered. #583 shipped it and a nightly test exercises it, so update the line in the same change.

Related: #1078, #829, #828, #583.

title: [TPU/Raiden/PD] Decode reshard handler exceptions are dropped by _listen; the room waits out the 300 s timeout instead of failing
body:
On the decode side, raiden's connector listener **logs and drops every exception raised by a message handler**. When a push-reshard handler raises (geometry construction, schedule building, chunk registration), the room is never failed. The request waits out `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT`, 300 s by default ([environ.py L702](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/environ.py#L702)), and only then fails. The log line has no room id and no traceback.

Code refs are permalinks at `c6067bab13`. `disaggregation/raiden/` is unchanged through `49959c5cf` (current `main`).

## Mechanism

1. **`_listen` catches and continues.** It logs `"RaidenKVManager message handling error: %s"` with `str(e)`: [conn.py L786-796](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/conn.py#L786-L796).
2. **The reshard chunk path has `try/finally` and no `except`.** A registration error escapes to `_listen` without failing the room: [receiver.py L681-699](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/receiver.py#L681-L699).
3. **The closing path never retries a deterministic error.** It marks the room registered *before* building the geometry, so a later message never rebuilds it: [receiver.py L1000-1021](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/receiver.py#L1000-L1021).

Two paths in the same code already handle errors correctly:
- Engine plan-registration errors record a failure on the room: [receiver.py L864-879](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/receiver.py#L864-L879).
- #748's `_on_pipeline_message` marks the room aborted and failed, then re-raises: [conn.py L830-850](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/conn.py#L830-L850). That is the pattern to reuse.

## Triggers

- **Today.** Any pool raiden can register but cannot build a reshard geometry for. For example, the 4-D MLA pool makes `head_pair_bytes` index `shape[4]` and raise `IndexError`. I'm filing the unsupported-config cases separately.
- **With #828.** Every topology #828 refuses. #828 raises its "refusal" from `ReshardGeometry.validate()` inside these per-room handlers. Operators see a 300 s stall per request and a log line, not a startup-time refusal. #829's arm J (`j-68a0d2c2`, HTTP 500) is consistent with this, but its job doesn't record the request latency.

## Suggested fix

- Wrap the decode reshard handlers (`RESHARD_CHUNK`, closing/finalize, SWA arm) the way `_on_pipeline_message` is wrapped: mark the room aborted and failed with the exception text, then re-raise or log with the room id and traceback.
- Separately, deterministic config errors (topology, layout, dtype) belong at bootstrap. The connector knows both sides' TP there, so it can fail fast once rather than per room.

## Test gap

The failure-handling tests only cover malformed tags: [test_raiden_failure_handling.py L94-103](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_raiden_failure_handling.py#L94-L103). No test raises from a reshard handler and asserts the room reaches `KVPoll.Failed`.

Related, not duplicates: #781 (prefill-side `_announce_chunk` send error, a different path), #772 (closed unmerged), #828, #829.

title: [TPU/Raiden/PD] P/D handshake does not compare KV pool layout: NHD and SEQ_ALONG_LANE peers exchange pages without error
body:
Prefill and decode each choose their TPU KV pool layout independently, either fused token-major (NHD) or `SEQ_ALONG_LANE` (HND). Nothing in the P/D handshake compares the two. When they differ, raiden copies pages between incompatible layouts as raw bytes. Depending on shape, the result is either fluent garbage with HTTP 200 or a failure on every request.

Code refs are permalinks at `c6067bab13`. The cited files are unchanged through `49959c5cf` (current `main`).

## How the layouts diverge

- The layout is a function of the attention backend plus an env flag. `SGLANG_TPU_USE_SEQ_ALONG_LANE_KV=1` only takes effect with `pallas_tpu_rpa_batched`: [tpu_platform.py L99-126](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/tpu/tpu_platform.py#L99-L126).
- So the layouts diverge if the flag is set on one side only. They also diverge if the flag is set on both sides but the backends differ (`rpa_v3` on one, `rpa_batched` on the other).

## Nothing compares them

- Bootstrap checks only `page_size` and `kv_cache_dtype`: [common/conn.py L958-974](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/common/conn.py#L958-L974).
- `ReshardReq` carries no layout, shape or head count: [serde.py L108-127](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/serde.py#L108-L127).
- Raiden's page copy is explicitly layout-agnostic: [kv_pool.py L512-514](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/tpu/kv_pool.py#L512-L514).
- #748 added `layout_fingerprint`, which hashes page shape, dtype, minor-to-major order and tiles, so it would distinguish NHD from HND: [pipeline.py L102-130](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/pipeline.py#L102-L130). It is compared only on the PP→TP pipeline path, inside tpu-sync's pool reshard planner. The symmetric pull path and the TP→TP push-reshard path never see it.

## Outcome at symmetric TP (pull path), page_size 256, head_dim 128

| KV dtype | kv-heads / rank | Page bytes, NHD vs HND | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | any | equal | accepted; KV is garbage |
| fp8 | ≥ 2 | equal | accepted; KV is garbage |
| fp8 | 1 | NHD pads 2 slots to 4, HND doesn't, so 2:1 | "Block transfer size mismatch"; every request fails |

This table assumes raiden's block size equals the logical page size. That holds on the code paths I read, but I haven't confirmed it on hardware. If it doesn't hold, more of these cases fail per request instead of passing garbage, and the issue stands either way.

## Suggested fix

- Have each side advertise its layout descriptor at bootstrap: layout name, `kv_packing`, per-rank heads, page bytes. The existing `layout_fingerprint` would do.
- Compare the descriptors for pull and push-reshard alike.
- Fail the affected requests with a clear message instead of raising. A `RuntimeError` at the existing bootstrap check site propagates out of the decode scheduler and takes the process down.

Note: #828 adds `dst_kv_layout` to `RESHARD_REQ`, which covers only the push-reshard path. #829's workaround #1 tells operators to flip this flag on both engines, which makes a mismatch more likely, not less.

Related: #829, #828, #344, #748.

title: [TPU/Raiden/PD] SWA KV is resharded with the full-attention kv-head count: silent SWA corruption for models with unequal SWA/full kv-heads (MiMo-V2, Gemma-4)
body:
SGLang-TorchTPU raiden P/D builds the **sliding-window (SWA) KV reshard geometry from the full-attention kv-head count**. For a model whose SWA layers have a different kv-head count than its full-attention layers, every asymmetric-attention-TP push-reshard and every PP→TP pipeline transfer writes the SWA KV to the wrong head offsets. Nothing errors and nothing goes out of bounds. This applies to **bf16 too**, not only fp8.

Code refs are permalinks at `c6067bab13`. Nothing under `disaggregation/raiden/` has changed through `49959c5cf` (current `main`).

## Where it happens

**TP→TP push-reshard.** `_make_geometry(..., swa=True)` takes the head-pair granule from the SWA tensor but the head count from `kv_args.total_kv_head_num`. Its docstring states the premise as fact: SWA layers "carry the same kv-head count as the full pool".
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/conn.py#L279-L308

**PP→TP pipeline (#748).** `head_slice_spans` gets the same single total for every pool, `swa.lN` included:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/pipeline.py#L663-L670

**The pool disagrees.** The SWA sub-pool is sized from `swa_num_key_value_heads`. Its comment names the case: "MiMo: num_key_value_heads=4 full vs swa_num_key_value_heads=8".
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py#L1757-L1774

## Affected models

| Model | Full kv-heads | SWA kv-heads | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| MiMo-V2 (on TPU since #129) | 4 | 8 | in-tree comment above |
| Gemma-4 (on TPU since #944) | `num_global_key_value_heads` | `num_key_value_heads` | remap in [config.py L218-242](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/config.py#L218-L242). Exact counts (e.g. 31B: 4 vs 16) come from the HF config, not in-tree |

GPT-OSS has equal counts, so it is not affected. The raiden README lists "hybrid sliding-window at symmetric TP and under push-resharding" as in scope ([README L84-85](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/raiden/README.md#L84-L85)).

## What lands where

I drove the in-tree `reshard_schedule.py` through a CPU byte model of the token-major (NHD) pool. This is a simulation, not a TPU run.

| Case (bf16, prefill attn TP8 → decode TP4) | SWA bytes correct | wrong | never written |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gemma-4 (SWA heads ≠ full) | 0% | 25% | 75% |
| MiMo-V2 (8 SWA vs 4 full) | 0% | 50% | 50% |
| Same, with the SWA head count passed in | 100% | 0% | 0% |

There are no out-of-bounds writes, so a bounds check on schedule entries would not catch this.

## Interaction with #828

- #828 does not change the SWA head count.
- MiMo fp8 SWA at 2→1 heads/rank is correct on `main` only because two errors cancel: fp8 `head_pair_bytes` is 2× too big, and the head count is 2× too small. #828 fixes the first error but not the second, so this case becomes silently wrong.
- With #828, Gemma-4 fp8 4→2 / 8→2 and MiMo fp8 4→2 also get false "partial FP8 head pack" refusals.
- This fix should land before #828 or together with it.

## Suggested fix

- Pass the SWA kv-head count for SWA pools on both paths.
- `ModelConfig.get_swa_num_kv_heads` already exists and is unused under `disaggregation/`: [model_config.py L1526-1537](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py#L1526-L1537).
- Carry it on `KVArgs` next to `total_kv_head_num`, or derive it per pool.
- Correct the `_make_geometry` docstring.

## Test gap

Both unit tests build SWA pools with the full head count, so they cannot see this:
- [test_tpu_reshard_layout.py L30-44](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/test/registered/unit/hardware_backend/tpu/test_tpu_reshard_layout.py#L30-L44)
- [test_raiden_pipeline.py L295-298](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-torchtpu/blob/c6067bab134f14420730be18a54e91ca57034edc/test/registered/unit/hardware_backend/tpu/test_raiden_pipeline.py#L295-L298)

No P/D e2e test runs a model with unequal head counts, so end-to-end reachability on hardware has not been exercised.

Related, not duplicates: #592 (introduced the equal-heads premise), #578, #944, #829.
